Assessor Tool · Sales Ratio Analysis

Sales Ratio Analysis

A complete ratio study from one sales file, run entirely in your browser. Measures assessment level, uniformity, and vertical equity against the IAAO Standard on Ratio Studies, with confidence intervals on every pass or fail. Stratifies by neighborhood, characteristic, or any column you choose, recommends neighborhood modifiers and land table or plat adjustments, and produces a printed study, an Excel workbook, a Board of Equalization packet, and a plain language view for commissioners and the public. Methods meet the IAAO Standard on Ratio Studies. Results support the assessor's own analysis and modifier decisions during the cycle; they do not replace the Department of Revenue's ratio study, which remains the official county ratio for equalization.

New here, or need the methodology behind a number? The user and methodology guide walks through every step, every statistic, and every setting, and each step below links to its section.

📖 User manual

Free, open-source, and private by design. Distributed by the Washington State Association of County Assessors for all 39 counties. One self-contained HTML file: no installation, no backend, and your sales data never leaves your browser. Methods follow the IAAO Standard on Ratio Studies; every decision rule is editable, every number is exportable, and a run manifest lets a second analyst reproduce the study to the digit. Created with AI assistance. Version adds bootstrap confidence intervals on COD and PRD, a significance test on the time trend, custom stratifiers, and the run manifest. Read the user and methodology guide for a walkthrough of every step and the reasoning behind each statistic; every step also links to its own section.

Step 1

Upload your sales file

CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file containing your validated sales. Sales should already be screened for arms-length transactions before upload — this tool does not perform sales validation. Multi-parcel sales should be pre-processed before upload (see the "How to read this" panel for the convention); rows with slash-separated values in the neighborhood or DOR-use columns will be dropped automatically.

What data this tool expects

Column headers can use any common naming — auto-detection handles most variations across CAMA systems. You'll confirm the mapping on the next step.

Required all four needed
  • Parcel ID — unique parcel identifier
  • Sale Price — validated arms-length sale price
  • Sale Date — any common date format or Excel serial
  • Total Assessed Value — current total AV
Optional each unlocks more analysis
  • Neighborhood — stratification & per-neighborhood modifier recommendations
  • Land AV + Improvement AV — split land/improvement modifier mode
  • DOR Primary Use, Land Table — additional stratification dimensions
  • Year Built, GLA, Acreage — stratification by decade, size bins, or acreage bands
  • Quality, Condition, Effective Age — stratification by construction grade, CDU rating, or age bands
  • Any other column — up to three custom stratifiers for dimensions this list does not cover, such as a zone, view, front footage, or traffic influence code

Step 3

Data summary

How your file was prepared for analysis. Rows excluded for missing required values or being part of a multi-parcel sale are shown here.

First 15 rows used in analysis

Showing parsed values after column mapping. Ratio is computed as Total AV ÷ Sale Price.

Step 4

Time adjustment

Trend in monthly median assessment ratios (AV ÷ SP) across your study period, fit by weighted least squares with each month weighted by its sales count so sparse months don't dominate the line. Ratios are the IAAO-recommended measure for time trend because assessed values are fixed as of the prior valuation date — drift in median ratio is therefore a direct read on market movement, free from the sales-mix shifts that distort median sale prices. Apply the trend to time-adjust every sale to a common reference date — typically January 1 of the assessment year — or leave it off and analyze unadjusted prices.

Step 5

Overall ratio diagnostics

IAAO standard ratio study statistics for the full sample. These numbers describe the appraisal level (median, mean, weighted mean), uniformity (COD, PRD), and vertical equity (IAAO 2025 Vertical Equity Indicator) of your current assessments relative to validated sales.

Step 6

Vertical equity analysis

Deeper vertical equity diagnostics beyond the headline VEI. The Coefficient of Price-Related Bias (PRB) and Spearman's rank-order correlation test for systematic relationships between assessment ratio and property value. The chart below visualizes each percentile group's median ratio with its 90% confidence interval against the overall sample median — the visualization IAAO recommends to accompany the VEI calculation.

Step 7

Stratified analysis

Same IAAO diagnostics run separately for each level of up to three stratifying variables. Available stratifiers depend on which optional columns you mapped — neighborhood, DOR primary use, land table, year built (decade bins), gross living area (data-driven quartile/decile or fixed 400-sq-ft bins), acreage (standard fixed bands or data-driven quartile/decile), quality, condition, and effective age. Stratification surfaces uniformity problems that the overall diagnostics smooth over — for example, drift across quality grades or condition codes often indicates a cost-table miscalibration. Strata with fewer than 10 sales are flagged as low-n so you check their confidence intervals before acting on them. IAAO sets no minimum stratum size; it directs that conclusions not be drawn from strata whose margins of error are too wide, and its first remedy for a thin stratum is to combine it with a similar one rather than to drop it or pad it with older sales.

Step 8

Modifier recommendations

Per-neighborhood suggested percent adjustments based on editable decision rules. The recommendation tells you how much to move each neighborhood's overall value level — apply it in your own CAMA system however your modifiers work. Rules pre-loaded with sensible defaults; edit any value (or load a saved preset) to see the table re-compute live.

Step 9

Report & export

Package the full analysis for archiving or sharing. The printable report opens in a new tab styled for letter-size paper — use your browser's "Print → Save as PDF" to save it. The Excel workbook contains separate sheets for the summary, modifier recommendations, vertical equity analysis, and each active stratification table.
